title: Use the vertex and symmetry of a parabola
subtitle: Nonlinear functions · 29 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **29 of the official questions in Nonlinear functions are this one** — 0 Easy, 3 Medium, 26 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- You're asked when a quadratic reaches its maximum or minimum, which value a coefficient could take given the vertex and the number of x-intercepts, or when a projectile comes back to a height it had earlier.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Get the vertex x-coordinate from x = −b/(2a), from vertex form, or as the midpoint of the two roots.
- 2) Use symmetry: a height reached at t₁ is reached again at 2·(vertex t) − t₁.
- 3) For 'could be the value' questions, write vertex form, check the direction of opening needed for the stated number of x-intercepts, then expand to test the coefficient.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph the quadratic and click the turning point to read the vertex.
Add a slider for any unknown constant and watch how the vertex and intercepts change.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You choose an x-intercept or the y-value of the vertex when the question asks for the x at the minimum.
You also get the sign in −b/(2a) or in vertex form (x − h) wrong, or you ignore that the parabola must open away from the axis to cross it twice.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You choose an x-intercept or the y-value of the vertex when the question asks for the x at the minimum.
You also get the sign in −b/(2a) or in vertex form (x − h) wrong, or you ignore that the parabola must open away from the axis to cross it twice.
